think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: An immunocompromised host (post-autologous stem cell transplantation for multiple myeloma) presenting with persistent fever and cough, who develops acute, severe thrombocytopenia (platelet count dropping from 123 to 30 x 10^9/L), rising serum creatinine, and gross hematuria. The core diagnostic challenge is establishing a diagnosis of dengue fever when initial NS1 antigen and serology are both negative, requiring clinical recognition of the characteristic laboratory trajectory and bleeding diathesis in an endemic setting.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The presentation ends after initial triage labs and imaging show persistent fever, cough, normal chest radiograph, baseline to acute platelet decline (123 to 30 x 10^9/L), acute renal impairment, and gross hematuria, immediately prior to send-out arboviral testing and inpatient nephrology intervention.
3. Differential Distinctions: Distinguishing arboviral infection from lower respiratory tract infection (ruled out by clear chest radiography), transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy or severe bacterial sepsis (ruled out by spontaneous stabilization and recovery with conservative hydration and supportive care without antimicrobial escalation), and primary renal or urological hemorrhage.
case_prompt: A 64-year-old man who had previously undergone autologous stem cell transplantation for multiple myeloma presented to the emergency department with persistent fever and cough. On initial evaluation, a plain chest radiograph was normal, showing no pulmonary infiltrates or consolidation. Baseline laboratory investigations revealed a precipitous drop in his platelet count from 123 × 10^9/L at baseline to 30 × 10^9/L. Concurrently, serum creatinine was elevated above baseline, and urinalysis demonstrated gross hematuria.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Lower Respiratory Tract Infection / Bacterial Pneumonia
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered given fever, cough, and post-transplant immunosuppression, but ruled out by unremarkable pulmonary imaging.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Transplant-Associated Thrombotic Microangiopathy or Severe Bacterial Sepsis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered given acute renal dysfunction, gross hematuria, and severe thrombocytopenia, but ruled out by spontaneous stabilization and recovery with hydration and supportive care alone.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: patient was managed conservatively with hydration, continuous bladder irrigation, and platelet transfusion support.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The characteristic trajectory of acute thrombocytopenia falling from baseline, bleeding manifestation (gross hematuria), and self-limiting course in a dengue-endemic region confirmed the clinical diagnosis despite negative initial viral antigen and serology.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Though dengue NS1 antigen and serology were negative, clinical and laboratory parameters favored the diagnosis of dengue fever.

editor_comments: Distilled admission teaching case for Dengue fever in a stem cell transplant recipient. Admission breakpoint enforced prior to viral serology/NS1 and management. Zero spoilers or pathogen names in case_prompt. Direct quotes verified.
